subproblem.title: Support, mass and boundary of a difference of currents
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ Euclid P and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n): spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B and M_W(A − B) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B). For all P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ Euclid P and A, B ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U): spt ∂A ⊆ spt A and ∂(A − B) = ∂A − ∂B.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (A - B).support ⊆ A.support ∪ B.support ∧ (A - B).massOn W ≤ A.massOn W + B.massOn W) ∧ ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), A.boundary.support ⊆ A.support ∧ (A - B).boundary = A.boundary - B.boundary
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the support and mass facts in the Notation paragraph of the parent proof ("spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B, spt ∂A ⊆ spt A", "|X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖") and the identity ∂Pc = ∂Q₀ − ∂(Q₀ − Pc) in step 7.

Definitions used.
 - (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) (the contract's Sub instance; this holds by rfl).
 - spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion T. Here zeroRegion T is the union of the open sets W' such that closure W' is compact, closure W' ⊆ U, and T vanishes on W' (T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W').
 - M_W(T) = sSup{ENNReal.ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W}. The admissible ω are the test forms on U with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm) for all x.
 - ∂T(γ) = T(dγ), where dγ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m γ has underlying form exteriorDerivative γ.

1. spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B. Let x ∈ spt(A − B), and suppose x ∉ spt A and x ∉ spt B. As x ∈ U, x lies in zeroRegion A and in zeroRegion B. So there are open sets W₁ ∋ x and W₂ ∋ x with compact closures contained in U, with A vanishing on W₁ and B vanishing on W₂. The set W₁ ∩ W₂ is open and contains x. Its closure is a closed subset of the compact set closure W₁, hence compact, and it lies in closure W₁ ⊆ U. A − B vanishes on W₁ ∩ W₂: if tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ ∩ W₂ then (A − B)(ω) = A ω − B ω = 0 − 0. So x ∈ zeroRegion(A − B), contradicting x ∈ spt(A − B).
2. M_W(A − B) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B). By sSup_le it suffices to bound ofReal((A − B)ω) for ω admissible for W. Then −ω is admissible too, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). By linearity, B(−ω) = −B(ω). Hence ofReal((A − B)ω) = ofReal(A ω + B(−ω)) ≤ ofReal(A ω) + ofReal(B(−ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, twice).
3. spt ∂A ⊆ spt A. Let x ∈ spt ∂A, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∈ zeroRegion A. This is witnessed by an open W₁ ∋ x, with compact closure ⊆ U, on which A vanishes. Then ∂A vanishes on W₁: if tsupport γ ⊆ W₁, then tsupport dγ ⊆ tsupport γ ⊆ W₁ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂A(γ) = A(dγ) = 0. Thus x ∈ zeroRegion ∂A, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ U ∖ zeroRegion A = spt A.
4. ∂(A − B) = ∂A − ∂B. For every test m-form γ, ∂(A − B)(γ) = (A − B)(dγ) = A(dγ) − B(dγ) = ∂A(γ) − ∂B(γ) = (∂A − ∂B)(γ), all by definition. Conclude by GeometricCurrentOn.ext. ∎
proof_key_steps: If x lies in open zero sets W₁ of A and W₂ of B (compact closures in U), then A − B vanishes on W₁ ∩ W₂.
For admissible ω, −ω is admissible and ofReal(Aω − Bω) ≤ ofReal(Aω) + ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B).
A zero set of A is a zero set of ∂A, since tsupport dγ ⊆ tsupport γ.
∂(A − B) = ∂A − ∂B pointwise by definition, then by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.

audit.reason: Intersecting relatively compact zero neighbourhoods proves the support inclusion; negated admissible forms prove the mass bound. Derivative support and pointwise linearity prove the boundary assertions for arbitrary U. The exact Lean proof independently checked.

subproblem.title: Divergence form of the exterior derivative along a coordinate face
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, b : Fin P → ℤ, and let γ be a C^∞ differential m-form on Euclid P (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), i.e. smooth, not analytic). Write e_i for the standard unit vectors, Φ(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (a map Euclid n → Euclid P) and E := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Let G : Euclid n → Euclid n satisfy G(y)_i = (−1)^i γ(Φ y)(e_{ι(succAbove i 0)}, …, e_{ι(succAbove i (m−1))}) for all y and i, i.e. γ(Φ y) evaluated on E with its i-th entry removed. Then: (1) G is C^∞; (2) ‖G(y)‖ ≤ |γ(Φ y)| (covectorEuclideanNorm) for all y; (3) dγ(Φ y)(E) = trace DG(y) for all y, where dγ = exteriorDerivative γ and trace DG(y) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ G y).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono ι → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) γ → (∀ (y : Euclid (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)), G y i = (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun l => EuclideanSpace.single (ι (Fin.succAbove i l)) (1 : ℝ))) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G ∧ (∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), ‖G y‖ ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm (γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))) ∧ ∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), exteriorDerivative γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the identity dγ'(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) = div G_F(y), with G_F(y)_j := (−1)^{j−1}γ'(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,ê_{i_j},…,e_{i_n}) and |G_F(y)| ≤ |γ'(φ_F y)|, in step 7 (34b) of the parent proof. The same computation is used in steps 5 and 8. Indices here are 0-based, so the sign is (−1)^i.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). c := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)). L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P is the continuous linear map L(y) := Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, e.g. Σ_j (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight e_{ι(j)}. So Φ(y) = c + L(y), Φ is C^∞, and Φ has derivative L at every point (L.hasFDerivAt.const_add c). Also L(e_i) = e_{ι(i)} for the unit vector e_i ∈ Euclid n. For i ∈ Fin n put w_i := (l ↦ e_{ι(succAbove i l)}) : Fin m → Euclid P, and ev_i := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ w_i, the continuous linear map α ↦ α(w_i) on Covector (Euclid P) m. Fin.removeNth i E = w_i holds definitionally. So the hypothesis on G reads G(y)_i = (−1)^i ev_i(γ(Φ y)).

1. Smoothness. y ↦ γ(Φ y) is C^∞, as a composition of C^∞ maps. Hence each coordinate y ↦ (−1)^i ev_i(γ(Φ y)) is C^∞, since ev_i is continuous linear. A map into Euclid n is C^∞ iff all its coordinates are (contDiff_euclidean), so G is C^∞.
2. Norm bound. Fix y and put α := γ(Φ y). Since ((−1)^i)² = 1, ‖G(y)‖² = Σ_i G(y)_i² = Σ_i α(w_i)² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). By definition, |α|² = Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(m−1)})² (covectorEuclideanNorm, where EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j = e_j).
 - The maps I_i := ι ∘ succAbove i (i ∈ Fin n) are strictly increasing, as compositions of strictly increasing maps (Fin.strictMono_succAbove).
 - They are pairwise distinct: if ι ∘ succAbove i = ι ∘ succAbove i', then succAbove i = succAbove i' because ι is injective, so i = i' (Fin.succAbove_left_injective).
 Since α(e_{I_i}) = α(w_i), Σ_i α(w_i)² is the sum of the nonnegative summands of |α|² indexed by the image {I_i} (Finset.sum_image). Hence it is ≤ |α|². Taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt) gives ‖G(y)‖ ≤ |α|.
3. Derivative of G. γ is differentiable, since it is C^∞; write Dγ := fderiv ℝ γ. By the chain rule, y ↦ (−1)^i ev_i(γ(Φ y)) has derivative v ↦ (−1)^i ev_i(Dγ(Φ y)(L v)) at y. Hence DG(y)(v) has i-th coordinate (−1)^i ev_i(Dγ(Φ y)(L v)) (hasFDerivAt_pi, composed with the linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ).symm).
4. Trace. Compute the trace in the standard basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply). Then trace DG(y) = Σ_i (DG(y)(e_i))_i = Σ_i (−1)^i ev_i(Dγ(Φ y)(L e_i)) = Σ_i (−1)^i (Dγ(Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}))(w_i).
5. Exterior derivative. γ is differentiable at Φ y, so SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply gives dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i (−1)^i • fderiv ℝ (x ↦ γ(x)(Fin.removeNth i E)) (Φ y) (E i). Since x ↦ γ(x)(Fin.removeNth i E) is ev_i ∘ γ, its derivative at Φ y is ev_i ∘ Dγ(Φ y), and E i = e_{ι(i)}. Hence dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i (−1)^i (Dγ(Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}))(w_i); the integer power acts by zsmul, (−1 : ℤ)^i • r = (−1 : ℝ)^i r.
6. Steps 4 and 5 give dγ(Φ y)(E) = trace DG(y) for every y. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves the statement. For m = 0, w_0 is the empty tuple, G(y)_0 = γ(Φ y)(()), and both sides of step 6 consist of the single term i = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ = c + L with L the continuous linear map y ↦ Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}; G(y)_i = (−1)^i ev_i(γ(Φ y)) with ev_i evaluation at E∘succAbove i, so G is C^∞ coordinatewise.
‖G(y)‖² = Σ_i γ(Φ y)(e_{ι∘succAbove i})²; the ι∘succAbove i are distinct strictly increasing indices, so this is a sub-sum of covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(Φ y))².
Chain rule: trace DG(y) = Σ_i (DG(y)e_i)_i = Σ_i (−1)^i Dγ(Φ y)(e_{ι(i)})(E∘succAbove i).
exteriorDerivative_apply gives the same alternating sum for dγ(Φ y)(E).

subproblem.title: Geometry of unit lattice faces: unit-cube volume, isometric face maps, diameter bound, separation of distinct faces
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ: (0) the open unit cube Q₁^k = {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} has Lebesgue measure 1. For all index pairs p = (ι, b), q = (ι', b') with ι, ι' : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing and b, b' : Fin P → ℤ, write Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (a map Euclid k → Euclid P; e_i the standard unit vectors). Then: (a) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y'; (b) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') ≤ √P whenever y, y' lie in the closed cube C^k = [0,1]^k; (c) if p ≠ q, y ∈ Q₁^k and y' ∈ C^k, then dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') ≥ 1, or dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) for some j.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1 ∧ ∀ p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → (∀ y y' : Euclid k, dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = dist y y') ∧ (∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ≤ Real.sqrt P) ∧ (p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (face notation, Hⁿ(F̆) = 1, diam F ≤ √P, and Lemma 2.1), written for faces of an arbitrary common dimension k, as the parent proof notes that Lemma 2.1 holds for j-faces of any common dimension.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) ∈ Euclid P. For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Q₁^k := {y : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}, C^k := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}. For v ∈ Euclid P, ‖v‖² = Σ_i v_i² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, EuclideanSpace.dist_eq), so |v_i| ≤ ‖v‖ for every coordinate i.

1. Volume. WithLp.ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and Q₁^k is the preimage under ofLp of the box Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1). Hence vol(Q₁^k) = Π_{i : Fin k} ENNReal.ofReal(1 − 0) = 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo). For k = 0 the empty product is 1.
2. Coordinates. EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 has i-th coordinate 1 if i = ι(j) and 0 otherwise, so Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j [ι(j) = i] y_j. Since ι is injective (strictly increasing), Φ_p(y)_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j and Φ_p(y)_i = b_i for i ∉ range ι.
3. (a) Isometry. By step 2, Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y') has coordinate y_j − y'_j at ι(j) and 0 at every i ∉ range ι, and each i is hit by at most one j. So ‖Φ_p y − Φ_p y'‖² = Σ_j (y_j − y'_j)² = ‖y − y'‖², i.e. dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y').
4. (b) Diameter. For y, y' ∈ C^k, |y_j − y'_j| ≤ 1 for all j, so dist(y, y')² ≤ k. Since ι : Fin k → Fin P is injective, k ≤ P. By (a), dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') ≤ √k ≤ √P.
5. (c) Set-up. Let p = (ι, b) ≠ q = (ι', b') with ι, ι' strictly increasing, y ∈ Q₁^k, y' ∈ C^k, x := Φ_p(y), z := Φ_q(y'). Then dist(x, z) ≥ |x_i − z_i| for every i.
6. Case A: some j has z_{ι(j)} ∉ (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)} + 1). Since x_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j with 0 < y_j < 1, every real number outside that open interval has distance ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) from x_{ι(j)}. Hence dist(x, z) ≥ |x_{ι(j)} − z_{ι(j)}| ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j): the second alternative holds.
7. Case B: b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1 for every j; in particular no z_{ι(j)} is an integer.
 (i) range ι ⊆ range ι': if ι(j) ∉ range ι', step 2 for q gives z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} ∈ ℤ, which is impossible. Both ranges have k elements, so they are equal, and two strictly increasing maps Fin k → Fin P with the same range coincide (each sends j to the (j+1)-st smallest element of the common range; formally by induction on j). So ι = ι'.
 (ii) b and b' agree on range ι: for each j, z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} + y'_j with y'_j ∈ [0, 1] and z_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ, so b'_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋; likewise b_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋ because b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1.
 (iii) Since p ≠ q and ι = ι', b ≠ b'; by (ii) there is i ∉ range ι with b_i ≠ b'_i. By step 2, x_i = b_i and z_i = b'_i are distinct integers, so dist(x, z) ≥ |b_i − b'_i| ≥ 1: the first alternative holds.
8. Cases A and B are exhaustive, which proves (c). For k = 0 there is no j, Case B applies with ι = ι' the empty map, and it gives dist(x, z) ≥ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: vol(Q₁^k) = 1: Q₁^k is the ofLp-preimage of the box Π(0,1) and ofLp is measure preserving (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
Coordinates: Φ_p(y)_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j and Φ_p(y)_i = b_i off range ι; hence Φ_p is an isometry and the closed face has diameter ≤ √k ≤ √P.
Separation, case A: if a coordinate z_{ι(j)} of the other point leaves (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)} + 1), the distance is ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
Case B: otherwise range ι ⊆ range ι', so ι = ι' and b, b' agree on range ι (floors); p ≠ q then gives distinct integers b_i ≠ b'_i off range ι and distance ≥ 1.

subproblem.title: Finitely many bounded integer polyhedral chains meet a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let K ⊆ Euclid P be compact, and let Λ ∈ ℝ. Consider the currents T ∈ 𝒟_k(Euclid P) (domain univ) for which there are a finite set s of index pairs p = (ι, b) (ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing, b : Fin P → ℤ) and integers β_p such that: Φ_p(y) ∈ K for some y ∈ [0,1]^k, for each p ∈ s; Σ_{p∈s}|β_p| ≤ Λ; and T(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{(0,1)^k} ω(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(k−1)}) dy for all test k-forms ω, where Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}. The set of such T is finite.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (Λ : ℝ), IsCompact K → {T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k | ∃ (s : Finset ((Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (β : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℤ), (∀ p ∈ s, StrictMono p.1) ∧ (∀ p ∈ s, ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ K) ∧ ∑ p ∈ s, |(β p : ℝ)| ≤ Λ ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, T ω = ∑ p ∈ s, (β p : ℝ) * ∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))}.Finite
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the "Finite family" paragraph of step 2 of the parent proof (the finite-family part of parent E0). The bounded integer coefficient vectors on the finitely many unit faces near the compact set K form a finite set, which is chosen before Q₀.

Notation. Q₁^k := {y ∈ Euclid k : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}; Cᵏ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), and [[p]](ω) := ∫_{Q₁^k} ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy. Since ι is injective, Φ_p(y)_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j and Φ_p(y)_i = b_i for i ∉ range ι. Let 𝒬 be the set in the statement.

1. K is compact, hence bounded: there is ρ ≥ 0 with |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ ρ for all x ∈ K and all i.
2. The set S_K := {p = (ι, b) : ι strictly increasing and Φ_p(y) ∈ K for some y ∈ Cᵏ} is finite. If Φ_p(y) ∈ K with y ∈ Cᵏ, then Φ_p(y)_i − b_i ∈ [0, 1] for each i (it is y_j if i = ι(j), and 0 otherwise), so |b_i| ≤ ρ + 1. Thus ι ranges over the finite type Fin k → Fin P, and b over the finite set {b : Fin P → ℤ : |b_i| ≤ ρ + 1 ∀ i} (Set.Finite.pi of the finite integer intervals). Let S_K also denote the corresponding Finset.
3. If Λ < 0 then 𝒬 = ∅, because Σ|β_p| ≥ 0 > Λ. So assume Λ ≥ 0. Then Z := {z ∈ ℤ : |z| ≤ Λ} is finite and contains 0, so the set 𝔅 of functions S_K → Z is finite.
4. For T ∈ 𝒬 choose witnesses (s, β) by classical choice. Then s ⊆ S_K, and |β_p| ≤ Σ_{q∈s}|β_q| ≤ Λ for p ∈ s. Define β̄_T ∈ 𝔅 by β̄_T(p) := β_p if p ∈ s and β̄_T(p) := 0 if p ∈ S_K ∖ s. Then T(ω) = Σ_{p∈S_K} β̄_T(p)[[p]](ω) for all ω, since the added terms vanish.
5. If T, T' ∈ 𝒬 have β̄_T = β̄_{T'}, then T(ω) = T'(ω) for all ω by step 4, so T = T' (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Thus T ↦ β̄_T is an injection of 𝒬 into the finite set 𝔅, and 𝒬 is finite (Finite.of_injective, or Set.Finite.of_finite_image). The degenerate dimensions k = 0, k > P and P = 0 need no change. ∎
proof_key_steps: Faces meeting the bounded set K have lower corners b in a finite box, so the admissible index pairs form a finite set S_K.
Each such T equals Σ_{p∈S_K} β̄_p[[p]] for some β̄ : S_K → {z ∈ ℤ : |z| ≤ Λ}, a finite set of coefficient vectors.
Currents are determined by their values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so T ↦ β̄ is injective and the set is finite.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes and unit orientations of subsets of a coordinate plane are ±e_ι
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, A ⊆ Euclid P, x ∈ Euclid P, Q a linear subspace of Euclid P, and ξ an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors). Assume a_i = x_i for every a ∈ A and every coordinate i outside the range of ι. Assume also that Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and that ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q). Then either ξ(α) = α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), StrictMono ι → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = x i) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = -α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (parent E7(a); Simon (26)). There, M ∩ F̆ ⊆ Π_F forces the approximate tangent plane to be V_F, and ξ(x) = ±e_F because two unit orientations of one n-plane differ by a sign. Here the step is isolated as a statement about approximate tangent planes (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and unit orientations.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ); E := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}); V := {v ∈ Euclid P : v_i = 0 for all i ∉ range ι}. Since ι is injective:
 - E is orthonormal (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single composed with ι, Orthonormal.comp);
 - V = span(range E) (expand v = Σ_i v_i e_i; the terms with i ∉ range ι vanish);
 - V is closed (finite-dimensional);
 - finrank V = n (finrank_span_eq_card for the linearly independent family E).

1. Blow-ups lie in V. For r > 0 and a ∈ A, blowUpMap x r a = r⁻¹ • (a − x), and (a − x)_i = 0 for i ∉ range ι by hypothesis. Hence S_r := blowUpMap x r '' A ⊆ V for every r > 0.
2. Q ⊆ V. Suppose q ∈ Q ∖ V. V is closed and nonempty, so d := infDist(q, V) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos), and ‖v − q‖ ≥ d for v ∈ V (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). Let f(y) := max(0, d/2 − ‖y − q‖). Then f is continuous, f ≥ 0, f > 0 exactly on ball(q, d/2), and f = 0 outside closedBall(q, d/2). So f has compact support and defines an element of C_c(Euclid P, ℝ). Also f = 0 on V.
 (i) Let r > 0. The set O := {f ≠ 0} = ball(q, d/2) is open, hence measurable, and disjoint from V ⊇ S_r. So (Hⁿ.restrict S_r)(O) = Hⁿ(O ∩ S_r) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply needs only O measurable; S_r need not be measurable). Hence f = 0 holds (Hⁿ.restrict S_r)-a.e., and ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ = 0.
 (ii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q gives Tendsto (r ↦ ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝(∫_Q f dHⁿ)). The function vanishes on (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, and 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ. By uniqueness of limits, ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.
 (iii) The same hypothesis gives finrank Q = n. Hence the support of Hⁿ.restrict Q is Q (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, SimonGMT Ch. 3). So the open neighbourhood ball(q, d/2) of q ∈ Q has positive (Hⁿ.restrict Q)-measure. Hⁿ.restrict Q is regular (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. So the continuous, compactly supported f is (Hⁿ.restrict Q)-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Since f ≥ 0 and support f = ball(q, d/2) has positive measure, ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). This contradicts (ii). Hence Q ⊆ V.
3. Q = V, because Q ≤ V and finrank Q = n = finrank V (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
4. Orientation. IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q gives an orthonormal τ : Fin n → Euclid P with span(range τ) = Q = V and a sign σ ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(α) = σ α(τ) for all n-covectors α. Both τ and E are orthonormal families of n vectors spanning the n-dimensional space V, so they define orthonormal bases bτ and bE of V indexed by Fin n. For an n-covector α let α_V be its restriction to V: the alternating map α.toAlternatingMap composed with the inclusion V.subtype. AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis bE gives α_V = α_V(bE) • bE.det. Hence α(τ) = α_V(bτ) = α(E) · bE.det(bτ). The scalar c := bE.det(bτ) does not depend on α, and c ∈ {1, −1} (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Therefore ξ(α) = (σc) α(E) for all α with a fixed sign σc ∈ {1, −1}. This is the claimed dichotomy, since α(E) is α applied to j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1.
5. The case n = 0 is included: V = {0} = Q, τ and E are both the empty family, α(τ) = α(E), and the dichotomy is exactly the one in IsUnitOrientationOf. ∎
proof_key_steps: All blow-ups blowUpMap x r '' A lie in the coordinate plane V = {v : v_i = 0 off range ι} = span{e_{ι(j)}}.
If q ∈ Q ∖ V, the bump f = (d/2 − |y − q|)⁺ vanishes on V, so its blow-up integrals are 0; but ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0 because supp(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Q. Hence Q ⊆ V, and Q = V by dimension.
For the orthonormal bases τ and e_ι of V, α(τ) = det_e(τ)·α(e_ι) with det_e(τ) = ±1 independent of α (eq_smul_basis_det); hence ξ = ±(α ↦ α(e_ι)).

audit.reason: The bump-function contradiction proves Q lies in the coordinate plane without requiring A measurable. Equal dimensions identify the planes, and the orthonormal change-of-basis determinant supplies one sign valid for every covector. The zero-dimensional case is covered.

subproblem.title: The (n−1)-skeleton of the unit lattice is Hⁿ-null
subproblem.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ the set L_m := {x ∈ Euclid P : there is a finite set s of coordinates with P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} (the points with at least P − m integer coordinates) satisfies μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), μHE[m + 1] {x : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof ("L_{n−1} (at least P − n + 1 integer coordinates) … has Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0", with n = m + 1). The parent's covering estimate is replaced by an equivalent argument that uses only lemmas available under the frozen imports: Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDimension is not imported, so dimH lemmas such as hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt are not used.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). L_m is the set in the statement.

1. Countable cover. For s : Finset (Fin P) and z : Fin P → ℤ put A(s, z) := {x ∈ Euclid P : ∀ i ∈ s, x_i = z_i}. Let x ∈ L_m with witness s. For i ∈ s, x_i is an integer, so x_i = ⌊x_i⌋. Hence x ∈ A(s, z) with z_i := ⌊x_i⌋. Therefore L_m ⊆ ⋃_{s : P ≤ m + |s|} ⋃_{z : Fin P → ℤ} A(s, z). The index set is countable (Finset (Fin P) is finite and Fin P → ℤ is countable). By measure_mono_null and measure_iUnion_null (used twice), it suffices to show μHE[m+1](A(s, z)) = 0 whenever P ≤ m + |s|.
2. Parametrization. Fix such s and z and let r := P − |s|, the number of coordinates outside s; then r ≤ m. Choose an injective κ : Fin r → Fin P whose range is the complement of s (e.g. the order embedding Finset.orderEmbOfFin of sᶜ). Define ψ : Euclid r → Euclid P by ψ(t) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => if i ∈ s then (z i : ℝ) else 0) + Σ_l t_l • e_{κ(l)}. Since κ is injective with values outside s, ψ(t)_i = z_i for i ∈ s and ψ(t)_{κ(l)} = t_l.
 - ψ is an isometry: ψ(t) − ψ(t') has coordinate t_l − t'_l at κ(l) and 0 elsewhere, so ‖ψ t − ψ t'‖ = ‖t − t'‖.
 - range ψ = A(s, z). "⊆" follows from the coordinate formula. For "⊇", let x ∈ A(s, z) and t_l := x_{κ(l)}; then ψ(t) and x agree at every i ∈ s (both equal z_i) and at every i ∉ s (i = κ(l) for some l).
 Hence A(s, z) = ψ '' univ.
3. Euclid r is μHE[m+1]-null. Euclid r = ⋃_{k : ℕ} closedBall 0 k (Metric.iUnion_closedBall_nat). By EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, μHE[r] = volume on Euclid r, so μHE[r](closedBall 0 k) = volume(closedBall 0 k) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top). Since r < m + 1, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (with d₁ := r, d₂ := m + 1 and the set closedBall 0 k) gives μHE[m+1](closedBall 0 k) = 0 or μHE[r](closedBall 0 k) = ∞. The second alternative is false, so μHE[m+1](closedBall 0 k) = 0 for every k. By measure_iUnion_null, μHE[m+1](univ : Set (Euclid r)) = 0.
4. Transfer. ψ is an isometry between Borel EMetric spaces, so Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image gives μHE[m+1](A(s, z)) = μHE[m+1](ψ '' univ) = μHE[m+1](univ : Set (Euclid r)) = 0.
5. Steps 1–4 give μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0. The argument covers P ≤ m (then s = ∅ is allowed and L_m = Euclid P) and P = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover L_m by the countably many coordinate affine planes A(s, z) = {x_i = z_i for i ∈ s}, with P ≤ m + |s| and z ∈ ℤ^P (z_i := ⌊x_i⌋).
Each A(s, z) is the image of an isometry ψ : Euclid r → Euclid P with r = P − |s| ≤ m.
Euclid r = ⋃ closedBall 0 k; μHE[r] = volume is finite on balls, so euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (r < m + 1) makes every ball μHE[m+1]-null.
Isometry invariance of μHE and countable subadditivity give μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0.

audit.reason: The countable affine-plane cover has dimensions r ≤ m. Finite measure on balls and the pinned zero-or-top lemma give H^(m+1)-nullity, which transfers through isometries. The proof includes P ≤ m and P = 0 without extra hypotheses.

subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, and let β assign an integer to each pair. Source: step 8 (boundary part) of the parent proof: "Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,1]ⁿ give [[F]](dγ) = Σ_j (−1)^{j−1}([[G_j^1]](γ) − [[G_j^0]](γ))", so ∂Pc is a finite integer combination of (n−1)-face currents. Indices here are 0-based, so the sign is (−1)^j. Uses the sibling face_divergence (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_divergence). The frozen contract does not import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem, so the cube identity is proved directly from Fubini and the one-variable fundamental theorem of calculus. All lemmas cited below are available under the frozen imports.

Notation.
 - n := m + 1; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ); Q₁^k := {y ∈ Euclid k : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}.
 - For p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P: Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), and [[p]](γ) := ∫_{Q₁^k} γ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy.
 - For j ∈ Fin n, t ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, ins_j(t, y') := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth j t (WithLp.ofLp y')) ∈ Euclid n: its j-th coordinate is t and the others are y' in order.
 - ∂T(γ) = T(dγ), where dγ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m γ has underlying form exteriorDerivative γ.

1. Faces of a face. For p = (ι, b) ∈ s, j ∈ Fin n and ε ∈ {0, 1} put q(p, j, ε) := (ι ∘ succAbove j, b + ε·𝟙_{ι(j)}), where (b + ε·𝟙_{ι(j)})_i := b_i + (if i = ι(j) then ε else 0).
 - ι ∘ succAbove j : Fin m → Fin P is strictly increasing.
 - Φ_{q(p,j,ε)}(y') = Φ_p(ins_j(ε, y')). Compare coordinates: at ι(j) both sides equal b_{ι(j)} + ε; at ι(succAbove j l) both equal b_{ι(succAbove j l)} + y'_l; at i ∉ range ι both equal b_i. Equivalently, expand Σ_{l : Fin n} with Fin.sum_univ_succAbove j.
 - E_{q(p,j,ε)} = E_p ∘ succAbove j = Fin.removeNth j E_p.
2. dγ as a divergence. Fix p ∈ s and a test m-form γ, which is C^∞. Define G : Euclid n → Euclid n by G(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (−1)^i γ(Φ_p y)(E_p ∘ succAbove i)). By face_divergence (ι := p.1, b := p.2), G is C^∞ and dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = trace DG(y) for all y. Computing the trace in the standard basis, trace DG(y) = Σ_i ∂_i G_i(y), where G_i(y) := G(y)_i is C^∞ and ∂_i h(y) := Dh(y)(e_i).
3. The cube identity. Claim: for every C^1 function h : Euclid n → ℝ and every i ∈ Fin n, ∫_{Q₁^n} ∂_i h(y) dy = ∫_{Q₁^m} (h(ins_i(1, y')) − h(ins_i(0, y'))) dy'. Proof:
 (a) Transport to Fin n → ℝ by the measure-preserving map WithLp.ofLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp). Q₁^n corresponds to the box B_n := Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1).
 (b) MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i : (Fin n → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ × (Fin m → ℝ), z ↦ (z_i, removeNth i z), has inverse (t, z') ↦ Fin.insertNth i t z'. It is measure preserving (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove), and it maps B_n onto Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B_m.
 (c) ∂_i h is continuous, hence bounded on the compact closed cube. So the integrand times the indicator of Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B_m is integrable for volume = volume.prod volume. Fubini (MeasureTheory.integral_prod_symm, or integral_prod followed by integral_integral_swap) gives ∫_{Q₁^n} ∂_i h = ∫_{z'∈B_m} ∫_{t∈Ioo 0 1} ∂_i h(toLp(insertNth i t z')) dt dz'.
 (d) Fix z'. The curve t ↦ toLp(insertNth i t z') has derivative e_i. By the chain rule, t ↦ h(toLp(insertNth i t z')) has derivative ∂_i h(toLp(insertNth i t z')), which is continuous in t. The fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, with ∫_{Ioo 0 1} = ∫_0^1 by MeasureTheory.integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo and intervalIntegral.integral_of_le) gives the inner integral h(toLp(insertNth i 1 z')) − h(toLp(insertNth i 0 z')).
 (e) Transport z' back to Euclid m by ofLp. For m = 0, B_0 and Q₁^0 = Euclid 0 are single points of measure 1, and the identity is the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0, 1].
4. Cubical Stokes. Apply steps 2–3 with h := G_i. All integrands are bounded continuous functions on bounded sets, so the finite sums may be exchanged with the integrals:
 ∫_{Q₁^n} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_{i∈Fin n} ∫_{Q₁^m} (G_i(ins_i(1, y')) − G_i(ins_i(0, y'))) dy'.
 By step 1, G_i(ins_i(ε, y')) = (−1)^i γ(Φ_{q(p,i,ε)} y')(E_{q(p,i,ε)}). Hence
 ∫_{Q₁^n} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_{i∈Fin n} (−1)^i ([[q(p,i,1)]](γ) − [[q(p,i,0)]](γ)).
5. Boundary of T. Applying the hypothesis on T to the test form dγ gives
 ∂T(γ) = T(dγ) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{Q₁^n} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_{p∈s} Σ_{i∈Fin n} Σ_{ε∈{0,1}} β_p (−1)^i (2ε − 1) [[q(p,i,ε)]](γ).
6. Regrouping. Let 𝒜 := s ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) ×ˢ {0, 1}, a finite set, with κ(p, i, ε) := q(p, i, ε) and c(p, i, ε) := β_p (−1)^i (2ε − 1) ∈ ℤ. Put s' := 𝒜.image κ and β'_q := Σ_{a∈𝒜, κ(a) = q} c(a) ∈ ℤ (β'_q := 0 for q ∉ s'). Every q ∈ s' has strictly increasing first component by step 1. Grouping the finite sum of step 5 by the value of κ (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to, or Finset.sum_image') gives Σ_{a∈𝒜} c(a)[[κ a]](γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q [[q]](γ), with the integer coefficients cast to ℝ. Therefore ∂T(γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} (β'_q : ℝ) ∫_{Q₁^m} γ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy for every test m-form γ, and s', β' do not depend on γ. ∎

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7 and 9 of the parent proof, namely the estimates (34a) and (34b) and the support bullets (Simon (29)–(30), (34)). Here they are proved for an arbitrary finite family of unit faces with integrable densities. Part (III)(b) uses the sibling face_divergence (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_divergence).

Notation.
 - n := m + 1; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ); Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}; Cⁿ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}.
 - For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), and F_p := Φ_p(Cⁿ).
 - For a test n-form ω, h_{p,ω}(y) := ω(Φ_p y)(E_p).
 - |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, and ‖α‖ is the operator norm of the continuous alternating map α.
 (F1) For a k-covector α and strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P, α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(k−1)})² is one of the summands defining |α|² (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = e_i). So |α(e_I)| ≤ |α|. Also |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π_j ‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖.
 (F2) A test form ω is continuous with compact support, so sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ < ∞ and sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞.

1. (I) Integrability. h_{p,ω} is continuous, because Φ_p is affine and evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is a continuous linear map. By (F1)–(F2), |h_{p,ω}| ≤ sup_x ‖ω(x)‖. Since w_p is integrable on Q₁, so is w_p · h_{p,ω} (Integrable.bdd_mul, after commuting the two factors).
2. (II) Existence. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n define L(ω) := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}.
 - Linearity: ω ↦ h_{p,ω} is linear and the integrands are integrable by (I), so L is linear (integral_add, integral_smul).
 - Bound: |L(ω)| ≤ (Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|) · sup_x ‖ω(x)‖.
 - Continuity: suppose TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then some compact K contains every tsupport ω_j. The iterated derivative of order 0 has norm ‖ω_j(x)‖ at x (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), so ω_j → 0 uniformly on K. Since ω_j = 0 off K, sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0, and the bound gives L(ω_j) → 0.
 So ⟨L, continuity⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn univ n, and D := ⟨L, continuity⟩ satisfies the displayed formula.
3. (III)(a) Mass. Let D satisfy the formula, and let ω be admissible for M(D) = M_univ(D), i.e. |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By (F1) with I = ι, |h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ |ω(Φ_p y)| ≤ 1, so D(ω) ≤ |D(ω)| ≤ Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|. Hence ofReal(D ω) ≤ ofReal(Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|) for every admissible ω. Taking the supremum (sSup_le) gives M(D) ≤ ofReal(Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|).
4. (III)(b) Boundary mass. Let B satisfy the hypothesis, and let γ be an admissible test m-form (|γ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). For p = (ι, b) ∈ s define G_p : Euclid n → Euclid n by G_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (−1)^i γ(Φ_p y)(E_p ∘ succAbove i)). γ is C^∞, being a test form. So face_divergence (with ι := p.1, b := p.2, γ and G := G_p) gives:
 - G_p is C^∞;
 - ‖G_p(y)‖ ≤ |γ(Φ_p y)| ≤ 1 for all y;
 - dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = trace DG_p(y) for all y, where dγ = exteriorDerivative γ is the form underlying exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m γ.
 Apply the formula for D to the test form dγ:
 ∂D(γ) = D(dγ) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y) · trace DG_p(y) dy ≤ Σ_{p∈s} |∫_{Q₁} w_p · trace DG_p| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} B_p.
 The last step is the hypothesis on B, which applies because G_p is C^∞ with |G_p| ≤ 1. So ofReal(∂D γ) ≤ ofReal(Σ_p B_p). Taking the supremum over admissible γ gives M(∂D) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} B_p).
5. (III)(c) Support. Let s* := {p ∈ s : ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0} and Z := ⋃_{p∈s*} F_p. Z is a finite union of continuous images of the compact set Cⁿ, so it is compact and hence closed.
 - For p ∈ s ∖ s*, w_p = 0 a.e. on Q₁ (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg). So the p-th summand of D(ω) is 0 for every ω.

subproblem.statement: Assume as a hypothesis (MR), exactly as in the selected theorem: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W whenever the IMRep R represents T on an open U. Let T ∈ 𝒟_k(Euclid P) (domain univ) satisfy T(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{(0,1)^k} ω(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(k−1)}) dy for all test k-forms ω, where Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}; for k = 0 this is evaluation at the lattice points b. Then T is integer multiplicity, M(T) = ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s}|β_p|), and T = 0 or M(T) ≥ 1.

Source: step 8 (first part) of the parent proof (parent E7(e)). The statement is written for faces of any dimension k ≥ 0, so that it also applies to the boundary chain of chain_boundary (k = m, including vertices when m = 0). Uses (MR) and the sibling face_geometry (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry).

Notation.
 - Hᵏ := μHE[k]; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ); Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid k : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}; Cᵏ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}.
 - For p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing: Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), F_p := Φ_p(Cᵏ).
 - Π_p := {x : x_i = b_i ∀ i ∉ range ι} = range Φ_p, and V_p := span(range E_p) = {v : v_i = 0 ∀ i ∉ range ι}. So for x ∈ Π_p, z ∈ Π_p ⟺ z − x ∈ V_p.
 - e_p := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_p ∈ MultiVector P k, i.e. α ↦ α(E_p).
 - δ_p(t) := min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)); this is 1 for k = 0.

1. Facts from face_geometry.
 - Φ_p is an isometry and vol(Q₁) = 1.
 - For distinct p, q ∈ s and t ∈ Q₁, every z ∈ F_q satisfies dist(Φ_p t, z) ≥ δ_p(t) > 0 (clause (c) with y' the preimage of z in Cᵏ; both alternatives are ≥ δ_p(t)).
 - In particular the sets F̆_p (p ∈ s) are pairwise disjoint.
2. Change of variables. Φ_p is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Measure.map Φ_p volume = Hᵏ.restrict (range Φ_p). Since F̆_p ⊆ range Φ_p and Φ_p⁻¹(F̆_p) = Q₁:

Index the finitely many p ∈ s⁺ by ℕ, padding with ∅, which is countably rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero. Then countablyRectifiable_iUnion shows that ⋃_{p∈s⁺} range Φ_p is countably k-rectifiable, and C is a subset of it (CountablyRectifiable.mono).

 - aestronglyMeasurable_orient: ξ is a finite sum of indicators of Borel sets times constants in the normed space MultiVector P k, hence strongly measurable.
4. Orientation and tangent plane at every x ∈ C. This gives the field orients, which only needs these facts a.e. on C. Let x ∈ F̆_p with p ∈ s⁺, write x = Φ_p(t) with t ∈ Q₁, and let δ := δ_p(t) > 0.

 (ii) C ∩ B(x, δ) = Π_p ∩ B(x, δ).
 - "⊆": a point z ∈ C ∩ B(x, δ) lies in F̆_q ⊆ F_q for some q ∈ s⁺. q ≠ p is impossible by step 1, since dist(x, z) < δ. So z ∈ F̆_p ⊆ Π_p.
 - "⊇": let z ∈ Π_p with |z − x| < δ, and put t'_j := z_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)}. Then z = Φ_p(t') (compare coordinates), and |t' − t| = |z − x| < δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) by the isometry. So 0 < t'_j < 1 and z ∈ F̆_p ⊆ C.
 (iii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x V_p. First, finrank V_p = k (finrank_span_eq_card; E_p is linearly independent). Let f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B(0, R). For 0 < r < δ/R, (blowUpMap x r '' C) ∩ B(0, R) = V_p ∩ B(0, R):

 - conversely, if v ∈ V_p and |v| < R, then z := x + r•v ∈ Π_p with |z − x| < δ, so z ∈ C by (ii) and v = blowUpMap x r z.
 The set blowUpMap x r '' C is Borel (the image of a Borel set under an affine homeomorphism), V_p is closed, and f vanishes off B(0, R). Hence ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' C} f dHᵏ = ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ for all 0 < r < δ/R. So the function r ↦ ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' C} f dHᵏ equals ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, which proves the required convergence. (For k = 0: V_p = {0}, Π_p = {b}, δ = 1, and the same computation holds.)
 Hence R := (C, θ, ξ) is an IMRep univ k.
5. R represents T. For a test k-form ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ. The integrand is bounded and C has finite measure. By disjointness (integral_biUnion_finset), the integral equals Σ_{p∈s⁺} ∫_{F̆_p} |β_p| sign(β_p) ω(x)(E_p) dHᵏ(x), which is Σ_{p∈s⁺} β_p ∫_{Q₁} ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy by step 2. Adding the zero terms with β_p = 0 gives T(ω). So R.Represents T, and T is integer multiplicity.

7. Dichotomy. If β_p = 0 for all p ∈ s, then T(ω) = 0 for all ω, so T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Otherwise some β_p is a nonzero integer, so |β_p| ≥ 1, and M(T) = ofReal(Σ_q |β_q|) ≥ ofReal(1) = 1.
8. If k > P there is no strictly increasing ι : Fin k → Fin P. Then s = ∅, C = ∅, T = 0 and M(T) = 0, and the steps above remain valid. ∎

subproblem.title: An integer multiplicity current carried by the n-skeleton is a finite sum of integer densities on open faces (Simon (26)–(28), (33))
subproblem.statement: Assume as hypotheses (VO), (MR) and (IMC), exactly as in the selected theorem. (VO): a current vanishes on test forms whose support is disjoint from its support. (MR): M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for open W when the IMRep R represents T on an open U. (IMC): (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces; (b) restricting an IMRep to a Borel set gives an IMRep that represents some current; (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity; (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x in the carrier. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, let K ⊆ Euclid P be compact, and let Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_n(Euclid P) (domain univ) be integer multiplicity with spt Q₀ ⊆ K and spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n := {x : ∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s}. Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof (parent E6 and E7(a); Simon (26)–(28), (33)). The face decomposition is read off from an integer multiplicity representation of Q₀, using the hypotheses (VO), (MR) and (IMC) and the siblings face_geometry, skeleton_null and plane_orientation (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry, Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_skeleton_null, Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_plane_orientation).

Notation.
 - n := m + 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ).
 - Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}; Cⁿ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}.
 - Index pairs. For p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and b : Fin P → ℤ, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Its coordinates are Φ_p(y)_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j and Φ_p(y)_i = b_i for i ∉ range ι.
 - E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), and e_p ∈ MultiVector P n is α ↦ α(E_p) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_p).
 - F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁) = {x : x_i = b_i for i ∉ range ι and b_{ι(j)} < x_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1 for all j}, a Borel set; F_p := Φ_p(Cⁿ), a compact set.
 - L_k := {x : ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ k + |s| ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, x_i ∈ ℤ}.
 - Z := zeroRegion Q₀ = Euclid P ∖ spt Q₀, an open set.

1. Representation. Q₀ is integer multiplicity, so fix R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep univ n with Q₀(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ for every test n-form ω. Here M is Borel; θ : Euclid P → ℕ is measurable, θ ≥ 1 on M, and ∫⁻_{M∩K'} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K'; ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ.restrict M. Let μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ.restrict M).withDensity θ.
2. Hⁿ(M ∩ Z) = 0. Let ω be admissible for M_Z(Q₀). Then tsupport ω ⊆ Z is disjoint from spt Q₀, so Q₀(ω) = 0 by (VO) (with U = univ, S = Q₀). Hence M_Z(Q₀) = 0. (MR) with U = univ and the open set W := Z gives μ(Z) = M_Z(Q₀) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∩ Z) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩Z} θ dHⁿ = μ(Z) = 0.
3. Hⁿ(L_m) = 0 by skeleton_null.
4. L_n ∖ L_m is covered by open faces. Let x ∈ L_n ∖ L_m and J := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}. From x ∈ L_n there is s ⊆ J with P ≤ n + |s| ≤ n + |J|. From x ∉ L_m, applied to s := J, we get P > m + |J|, i.e. P ≥ n + |J|. So the complement I := Fin P ∖ J has exactly n elements. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P be its strictly increasing enumeration (Finset.orderEmbOfFin), b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ for all i, and y_j := x_{ι(j)} − ⌊x_{ι(j)}⌋. Since x_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ, 0 < y_j < 1, so y ∈ Q₁. Also x = Φ_{(ι,b)}(y) coordinatewise: for i ∈ J, x_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = b_i.
5. The finite index set. Let S := {p = (ι, b) : ι strictly increasing and Φ_p(y) ∈ spt Q₀ for some y ∈ Q₁}. K is compact, so there is ρ with |x_i| ≤ ρ for all x ∈ K and all i. If Φ_p(y) ∈ spt Q₀ ⊆ K with y ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cⁿ, then Φ_p(y)_i − b_i ∈ [0, 1] for all i, so |b_i| ≤ ρ + 1. There are finitely many maps Fin n → Fin P and finitely many b with all |b_i| ≤ ρ + 1, so S is finite; let s be the corresponding Finset (Set.Finite.toFinset). Every p ∈ s has ι strictly increasing and some y ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cⁿ with Φ_p(y) ∈ spt Q₀; these are two of the required conclusions. (If n > P then s = ∅.)
6. Disjointness. For distinct p, q ∈ s, F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅. Indeed, suppose Φ_p(y) = Φ_q(y') with y, y' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cⁿ. Clause (c) of face_geometry gives dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') ≥ 1, or ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) > 0 for some j. Either way the distance is positive, a contradiction.
7. M is covered up to a null set. Let x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_{p∈s} F̆_p. If x ∉ spt Q₀ then x ∈ M ∩ Z. Otherwise x ∈ spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n. If moreover x ∉ L_m, step 4 gives p with x = Φ_p(y), y ∈ Q₁; then p ∈ s because x ∈ spt Q₀, contradicting x ∉ F̆_p. Hence M ∖ ⋃_{p∈s} F̆_p ⊆ (M ∩ Z) ∪ L_m, which is Hⁿ-null by steps 2 and 3.
8. Change of variables. By face_geometry (a), Φ_p is an isometry Euclid n → Euclid P. Hence it is a closed embedding and a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Measure.map Φ_p volume = Hⁿ.restrict (range Φ_p). We have F̆_p ⊆ range Φ_p, and Φ_p⁻¹(F̆_p) = Q₁ by injectivity. So MeasurableEmbedding.setIntegral_map and its lintegral analogue give:
 - ∫_{F̆_p} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy for every h integrable on F̆_p;
 - ∫⁻_{F̆_p} h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy for measurable h ≥ 0.
9. Orientation on a face. Fix p = (ι, b) ∈ s. Apply (IMC)(b) to R and the Borel set E := F̆_p (U = univ is open). It gives R' : IMRep univ n with R'.carrier = M ∩ F̆_p and R'.orient = ξ. By R'.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F̆_p there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ F̆_p) x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q; we may also assume x ∈ M ∩ F̆_p (ae_restrict_mem). Every a ∈ A := M ∩ F̆_p satisfies a_i = b_i = x_i for i ∉ range ι. So plane_orientation (with ι, A, x, Q, ξ x) gives ξ(x) = e_p or ξ(x) = −e_p as functionals, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F̆_p.
10. Densities. Let ξ̃ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ. It is strongly measurable, and ξ̃ = ξ holds (Hⁿ.restrict M)-a.e. For p ∈ s define σ_p(x) := 1 if ξ̃(x) = e_p; σ_p(x) := −1 if ξ̃(x) ≠ e_p and ξ̃(x) = −e_p; and σ_p(x) := 0 otherwise. The sets {ξ̃ = e_p} and {ξ̃ = −e_p} are measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun against constants), so σ_p is measurable. Define u_p(y) := 1_M(Φ_p y) · θ(Φ_p y) · σ_p(Φ_p y) for p ∈ s, and u_p := 0 for p ∉ s. Each u_p is measurable and u_p(y) ∈ ℤ for every y. Note e_p ≠ −e_p: e_p(α_p) = 1 for the n-covector α_p(v) := det[(v_j)_{ι(k)}]. So by step 9 and ξ̃ = ξ a.e., ξ(x) = σ_p(x) e_p for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F̆_p. Hence θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) = θ(x) σ_p(x) ω(x)(E_p) there, for every test form ω.
11. Integrability and mass. For p ∈ s, |u_p(y)| ≤ (1_M θ)(Φ_p y). By step 8, ∫⁻_{Q₁} |u_p| ≤ ∫⁻_{F̆_p} 1_M θ dHⁿ = μ(F̆_p) ≤ μ(F_p) < ∞, since F_p is compact (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). So u_p is integrable on Q₁. By steps 6 and 8 and (MR) with W = univ:
 Σ_{p∈s} ofReal(∫_{Q₁}|u_p|) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫⁻_{Q₁}|u_p| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} μ(F̆_p) = μ(⋃_{p∈s} F̆_p) ≤ μ(univ) = M_univ(Q₀) = M(Q₀).
 The integrals are ≥ 0, so ofReal(Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|u_p|) = Σ_p ofReal(∫_{Q₁}|u_p|) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg). Hence ofReal(Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|u_p|) ≤ M(Q₀).
12. The representation. Fix a test n-form ω and let g(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)). g is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ.restrict M. By (IMC)(d), |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M. The function x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous with compact support, so it is bounded by some C_ω and vanishes off tsupport ω. Thus |g| ≤ C_ω θ 1_{tsupport ω} a.e. on M. The right side has finite integral (locallyIntegrable_mult with K' := tsupport ω), so g is integrable on M.
 - By step 7, ∫_M g dHⁿ = ∫_{⋃_{p∈s}(M∩F̆_p)} g dHⁿ.
 - The sets M ∩ F̆_p are pairwise disjoint and measurable (step 6), so this equals Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{M∩F̆_p} g dHⁿ (integral_biUnion_finset).
 - For p ∈ s, step 10 gives ∫_{M∩F̆_p} g dHⁿ = ∫_{F̆_p} 1_M θ σ_p ω(·)(E_p) dHⁿ, which equals ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y) ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy by step 8.
 Hence Q₀(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y) ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy.
13. Steps 5, 10, 11 and 12 give every conclusion:
 - s is finite and each ι is strictly increasing;
 - each closed face F_p meets spt Q₀;
 - each u_p is integer-valued everywhere and integrable on Q₁;
 - the mass bound and the representation formula hold. ∎

Every x ∈ L_n ∖ L_m is Φ_p(y) with y ∈ Q₁ (ι = the non-integer coordinates, b = ⌊x⌋). The faces whose open face meets spt Q₀ form a finite set s; distinct open faces are disjoint (face_geometry); so M ⊆ ⋃_{p∈s} F̆_p up to an Hⁿ-null set.

Source: step 5 of the parent proof (parent E7(b); Simon (27)–(28), (32)). There the variation of the density on a face is bounded by Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) for explicit pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods N_F, and Σ_F Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀). The support part is the argument of step 9: Var_F > 0 implies that F meets spt ∂Q₀. Uses the hypothesis (VO) and the siblings face_geometry, face_divergence, face_integral_current and current_calculus (Lean names Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry, …_face_divergence, …_face_integral_current, …_current_calculus).

Notation.
 - n := m + 1; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ); Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}; Cⁿ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}.
 - Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}), F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), F_p := Φ_p(Cⁿ).
 - For p = (ι, b) let p̃_p : Euclid P → Euclid n be p̃_p(x)_j := x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)}. It is continuous and affine (C^∞), and p̃_p(Φ_p y) = y.
 - δ(t) := min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)) for t ∈ Euclid n. δ is continuous, and δ(t) > 0 for t ∈ Q₁.
 - |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
 - For an m-current S on univ and a set W, M_W(S) = sSup{ofReal(S γ) : γ ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m W}; the admissible γ are the test forms with tsupport γ ⊆ W and |γ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. M(S) = M_univ(S).

1. Neighbourhoods. For p ∈ s let N_p := {x : p̃_p(x) ∈ Q₁ and dist(x, Φ_p(p̃_p x)) < δ(p̃_p x)/2}. N_p is open, because Q₁ is open, all maps involved are continuous, and the inequality is strict. F̆_p ⊆ N_p: for x = Φ_p(y) with y ∈ Q₁, p̃_p(x) = y and the distance is 0.
 (i) N_p ∩ F_q = ∅ for q ∈ s with q ≠ p. Suppose x ∈ N_p and x = Φ_q(y') with y' ∈ Cⁿ, and put t := p̃_p(x) ∈ Q₁. Clause (c) of face_geometry (for the pairs p ≠ q, t ∈ Q₁ and y' ∈ Cⁿ) gives dist(Φ_p t, x) ≥ 1, or dist(Φ_p t, x) ≥ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for some j. In both cases dist(Φ_p t, x) ≥ δ(t), contradicting dist(x, Φ_p t) < δ(t)/2.
 (ii) N_p ∩ N_q = ∅ for distinct p, q ∈ s. Suppose x lies in both. Put t := p̃_p x and t' := p̃_q x (both in Q₁), y := Φ_p t and y' := Φ_q t'. Clause (c) for (p, q, t, t') gives dist(y, y') ≥ δ(t), and clause (c) for (q, p, t', t) gives dist(y', y) ≥ δ(t'). But dist(y, y') ≤ dist(y, x) + dist(x, y') < δ(t)/2 + δ(t')/2 ≤ max(δ(t), δ(t')), a contradiction.
2. Supports. Apply face_integral_current to s and w := u (its hypotheses are among ours), and use part (III)(c) with D := Q₀ (its formula is our hypothesis). It gives: every x ∈ spt Q₀ equals Φ_q(y) for some q ∈ s and y ∈ Cⁿ. By current_calculus, spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ spt Q₀. Hence every point of spt ∂Q₀ lies in F_q for some q ∈ s.
3. Definition of V. M_{N_p}(∂Q₀) ≤ M(∂Q₀) < ∞ (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono). Put V_p := (M_{N_p}(∂Q₀)).toReal ≥ 0 for p ∈ s, and V_p := 0 otherwise. For every γ admissible for N_p, ofReal(∂Q₀ γ) ≤ M_{N_p}(∂Q₀) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since this mass is finite, ∂Q₀(γ) ≤ V_p.
4. Coordinate covectors. For J : Fin m → Fin P let dx^J be the m-covector (v_0, …, v_{m−1}) ↦ det[(v_a)_{J(c)}]_{a,c}. It is the alternating map Matrix.detRowAlternating composed with the linear map v ↦ (v_{J(c)})_c, made continuous by finite dimensionality (e.g. AlternatingMap.mkContinuous with a bound from finite dimensionality).
 - For strictly increasing I, J : Fin m → Fin P, dx^J(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(m−1)}) = 1 if I = J and 0 otherwise. The matrix [(e_{I(a)})_{J(c)}] = [I(a) = J(c)] is the identity if I = J. If I ≠ J, then range I ≠ range J (strictly increasing maps with equal ranges coincide), so some I(a) ∉ range J and row a vanishes.
 - For j ∈ Fin n let ε_j := (−1)^j dx^{ι∘succAbove j}. The maps ι ∘ succAbove j are strictly increasing and pairwise distinct, because ι is injective and Fin.succAbove is injective in its first argument.
 Hence, for reals c_j, (Σ_j c_j ε_j)(e_I) = (−1)^j c_j if I = ι ∘ succAbove j, and 0 for every other strictly increasing I. Consequently |Σ_j c_j ε_j|² = Σ_j c_j², and (Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'})(E_p ∘ succAbove i) = (−1)^i c_i. (For m = 0, ι ∘ succAbove 0 is the empty map and ε_0 is the constant 0-covector 1.)
5. The test form for g. Fix p ∈ s and g as in (i). If tsupport g = ∅ then g = 0, the integral is 0, and 0 ≤ V_p; so assume tsupport g ≠ ∅.
 - Kg := Φ_p(tsupport g) is compact (g has compact support), and Kg ⊆ F̆_p ⊆ N_p.
 - Choose r > 0 with cthickening(3r, Kg) ⊆ N_p (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
 - Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (order ⊤ : ℕ∞, i.e. C^∞) to the open set thickening(2r, Kg) and the closed set cthickening(r, Kg) ⊆ thickening(2r, Kg). It gives a C^∞ map χ : Euclid P → [0, 1] with support χ = thickening(2r, Kg). So tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r, Kg) ⊆ N_p is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). Also χ = 1 on cthickening(r, Kg), hence on the open neighbourhood thickening(r, Kg) of Kg.
 Put γ(x) := χ(x) · Σ_j g_j(p̃_p x) ε_j. γ is C^∞ and tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ N_p is compact, so γ is a test m-form on univ. By step 4, |γ(x)| = χ(x) ‖g(p̃_p x)‖ ≤ 1. So γ is admissible for N_p, and ∂Q₀(γ) ≤ V_p by step 3.
6. dγ on the face p. Let G := (y ↦ χ(Φ_p y) • g(y)) : Euclid n → Euclid n. By step 4 and p̃_p(Φ_p y) = y, (−1)^i γ(Φ_p y)(E_p ∘ succAbove i) = (−1)^i χ(Φ_p y) Σ_j g_j(y) ε_j(E_p ∘ succAbove i) = χ(Φ_p y) g_i(y) = G(y)_i for all y and i. So face_divergence (ι := p.1, b := p.2, γ, G) gives dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = trace DG(y) for all y. Moreover trace DG(y) = trace Dg(y) for every y:
 - The open set O := Φ_p⁻¹(thickening(r, Kg)) contains tsupport g, and χ∘Φ_p = 1 on O. So G = g on O, and DG(y) = Dg(y) for y ∈ O (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
 - If y ∉ O then y ∉ tsupport g, so g and G = (χ∘Φ_p)·g both vanish on a neighbourhood of y, and DG(y) = 0 = Dg(y).
 Hence dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = trace Dg(y) for all y.
7. Other faces. For q ∈ s with q ≠ p and y ∈ Q₁, Φ_q(y) ∈ F_q. F_q is disjoint from N_p by step 1(i), and N_p ⊇ tsupport γ ⊇ tsupport dγ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). So dγ(Φ_q y) = 0.
8. Bound (i). Apply the formula for Q₀ to the test form dγ and use steps 6–7: ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ) = Σ_{q∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_q(y) dγ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy = ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y) trace Dg(y) dy. With step 5 this proves ∫_{Q₁} u_p · trace Dg ≤ V_p.
9. Sum bound. Let η > 0. For each p ∈ s choose γ_p admissible for N_p with ∂Q₀(γ_p) ≥ V_p − η. If V_p ≤ η take γ_p := 0. Otherwise ofReal(V_p − η) < ofReal(V_p) = M_{N_p}(∂Q₀), so lt_sSup_iff supplies an admissible γ_p with ofReal(∂Q₀ γ_p) > ofReal(V_p − η), hence ∂Q₀(γ_p) > V_p − η. Put γ := Σ_{p∈s} γ_p, a test m-form. At each x at most one γ_p(x) is nonzero: γ_p(x) ≠ 0 forces x ∈ tsupport γ_p ⊆ N_p, and the N_p are pairwise disjoint (step 1(ii)). So |γ(x)| ≤ 1, and γ is admissible for univ. Hence Σ_{p∈s}(V_p − η) ≤ Σ_p ∂Q₀(γ_p) = ∂Q₀(γ) ≤ M(∂Q₀).toReal (step 3 with W = univ). Letting η → 0 gives Σ_{p∈s} V_p ≤ M(∂Q₀).toReal. Since M(∂Q₀) < ∞, ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} V_p) ≤ M(∂Q₀).
10. Support (ii). Let p ∈ s with V_p ≠ 0. Then M_{N_p}(∂Q₀) ≠ 0, so by lt_sSup_iff some γ admissible for N_p has ofReal(∂Q₀ γ) > 0, i.e. ∂Q₀(γ) ≠ 0. By (VO) applied to S := ∂Q₀ (degree m, U = univ), tsupport γ is not disjoint from spt ∂Q₀. Take x ∈ tsupport γ ∩ spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ N_p ∩ spt ∂Q₀. By step 2, x ∈ F_q for some q ∈ s, and q = p by step 1(i). So x = Φ_p(y) with y ∈ Cⁿ and x ∈ spt ∂Q₀.
11. Steps 3 and 8–10 give all conclusions: V_p ≥ 0 for p ∈ s, ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} V_p) ≤ M(∂Q₀), the bound (i), and the support statement (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Open neighbourhoods N_p ⊇ F̆_p with N_p ∩ F_q = ∅ (q ≠ p), pairwise disjoint, from face_geometry separation; spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ spt Q₀ ⊆ ⋃_q F_q by current_calculus and face_integral_current (III)(c).
V_p := M_{N_p}(∂Q₀).toReal (finite) bounds ∂Q₀(γ) for every admissible γ supported in N_p.

For g, γ := χ Σ_j g_j(p̃_p ·) (−1)^j dx^{ι∘succAbove j} is admissible in N_p; face_divergence and χ = 1 near Φ_p(tsupport g) give dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = div g(y), and dγ vanishes on the other faces, so ∫ u_p div g = ∂Q₀(γ) ≤ V_p.
Summing near-optimal forms over the disjoint N_p gives Σ V_p ≤ M(∂Q₀); if V_p ≠ 0, (VO) gives a point of spt ∂Q₀ in N_p, which must lie on F_p.

audit.reason: Face separation proves the neighbourhoods are disjoint. The explicit cutoff forms recover the divergence tests with norm at most one; near-optimal forms give the sum bound. The support conclusion follows from VO and the declared support dependencies, without an omitted skeleton-support or boundary-measure hypothesis.
